A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same VibeCheck paper, with 29 readable pages and complete Appendices A–H. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison; all appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: v6 reports original VibeCheck evaluations, including model-matching and preference-prediction results in Table 2 and analyses of summarization, mathematical reasoning, and captioning in Section 6 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v7 retains these original evaluations and their reported outcomes in Table 2, Section 6, and Appendix G.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix D retain the same discovery, vibe reduction, judge scoring, filtering, logistic regression, and iterative refinement procedures. No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HC3, Chatbot Arena overall and its STEM/Writing subsets, CNN/DailyMail, MATH, and COCO captions. The revised MMLU background discussion introduces no evaluated dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same Predefined Vibes comparator and VibeCheck iteration variants, and Table 4 retains every evaluated model pair. Removing Claude-3-Sonnet and Gemini 1.5 from the background paragraph does not remove evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, preference judges, data splits in Table 3, and hyperparameters in Table 5 are unchanged. The Section 6 description of cached HELM predictions and 1,000 COCO images moves across a page boundary without changing the protocol.

E4.justification: The iteration comparison in Table 2, task-specific analysis in Figure 3, judge-error examples in Appendix F, and illustrative cases in Appendix H are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: No run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance procedures are added or revised. References to regression p-values and the limitation concerning run-to-run variability remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 5.2 replaces the background statement that Llama-3-70b outperforms Claude-3-Sonnet and Gemini 1.5 on MMLU with a statement that GPT-4 and Claude 3 Opus outperform Llama on conventional benchmarks despite similar Arena preferences. This changes a contextual ranking comparison involving different model pairs. VibeCheck's own results are unchanged, including Table 2's three-iteration overall accuracies of 80.34% for model matching and 59.34% for preference prediction.

T1.justification: The vibe-score definition, separability equation, and classifier-based definitions in Sections 3–4 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and claims about discovering, quantifying, and interpreting model vibes. The abstract's resource-access update does not change these claims.

C2.justification: The revised Arena motivation foregrounds the benchmark–preference discrepancy already discussed in v6. The interpretation that qualitative traits may explain user preferences, task-specific explanations, and limitations in Section 7 and Appendix F remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the direct VibeCheck GitHub code pointer with bench-mark.org and explicitly advertises a vibe visualizer alongside the code. This changes documented access information; implementation details and prompts remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the website's functionality.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to earlier research in Section 2 and Appendix E are unchanged. The Llama 3 model-card reference receives only a punctuation correction.

P1.justification: v7 repairs the awkward evaluation-description sentence in Section 5, trims the opening of Section 5.1, and condenses the background and setup paragraphs in Section 5.2. Section organization and the remaining narrative are preserved.

P2.justification: Spacing and text reflow shift existing tables, figures, and example panels within pages 6–10. Figure 2 moves upward, allowing the Section 6 opening paragraph to fit on page 7, and spacing around Table 2 changes. Display content, captions, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v7 makes the Arena motivation more direct, improves a few awkward passages, and adds explicit visualizer access information. These are limited readability and documentation gains, with the experimental evidence and limitations preserved. The PDFs do not establish improved empirical support or verify the advertised website's functionality.
